parts:
Hello,

first of all a big thank you to the developers of the shiny package - it really does make my life a lot easier! I am analysing biological data and being able to convert my R-scripts into interactive applications allows the biologists to explore their data and I can focus on developing and implementing new ways to analyse the data! I also want to thank people who reply to posts in this group. I have found many useful suggestions here.

I have a question that I could not find an answer to. I have been trying for two days to solve a problem that seems very simple: after uploading and reading in a number of data files in a zip-archive, I want to generate a plot for each of these files. The number of files can vary between 1 and 20 (or more). The problem is that the plot for each file already consists of 8x12 plots (par(mfrow=c(8,12))). I tried using split.screen with plotOutput, but that keeps giving me "figure margins too large"-error messages even when I adjust the plot area size to dimensions that I know should work. I also tried generating pngs and an html page, but when I use includeHTML, the images do not show up - should relative paths work? They do for the data file operations, but not when I am trying to include images via html (I tried both, runApp() locally and on a shiny-server).

My question is actually very similar to this one: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/15875786/dynamically-add-plots-to-web-page-using-shiny - but there is no reply yet. From the example in the post I got the idea to play around with uiOutput and renderUi but did not get that two work either.

I would be grateful for any pointers as to how this should be approached.

Thank you very much for your time :-)
Michaela

parts:
Here is functional code to make a variable number of plots based on the number of columns.  I suggest using this as a starting point, and adding small amounts of code until you pinpoint what exactly is breaking it.

server.r:
max_plots <- 100
library(shinyIncubator)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

sampletable=reactive({
if(input$go<1)
return()

x1=c(106:110, 21:25)
x2=c(101:105, 201:205)
x3=c(21:25, 31:35)
x4=c(51:60)
input$go
x=isolate(rbind(x1,x2,x3,x4))

x
})
  # Insert the right number of plot output objects into the web page
  output$plots <- renderUI({
    plot_output_list <- lapply(1:ncol(sampletable()), function(i) {

plotname <- paste("plot", i, sep="")
      plotOutput(plotname, height = 280, width = 250)
    })

# Convert the list to a tagList - this is necessary for the list of items
    # to display properly.
    do.call(tagList, plot_output_list)
  })

  # Call renderPlot for each one. Plots are only actually generated when they
  # are visible on the web page.
  for (i in 1:max_plots) {
    # Need local so that each item gets its own number. Without it, the value
    # of i in the renderPlot() will be the same across all instances, because
    # of when the expression is evaluated.
    local({
      my_i <- i
      plotname <- paste("plot", my_i, sep="")

      output[[plotname]] <- renderPlot({
        plot(sampletable()[,my_i], sampletable()[,my_i],
             xlim = c(min(sampletable()[,my_i]), max(sampletable()[,my_i])),
             ylim = c(min(sampletable()[,my_i]), max(sampletable()[,my_i])),
             main = "look at all those things"        )
      })
    })
  }
})

ui.r

library(shinyIncubator)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel("Dynamic number of plots"),

  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput("n", "this isn't used, I used the ncol function instead, but feel free to move the slider for fun.", value=1, min=1, max=5),
  actionButton("go", "Update")
  ),

  mainPanel(
    # This is the dynamic UI for the plots
    uiOutput("plots")
  )
))
